label: thm:non-explicit
title: Existence of multi-seed-protecting extractors against noncolluding entropy-preserving adversaries
difficulty_reason: The existence proof has to control random extractor evaluations that overlap across several noncolluding tampering functions, so its main concentration argument cannot assume independent samples. The authors build a bounded-degree collision graph, partition its seeds into independent classes, and establish the conditional mean-zero property needed for separate martingale bounds on both the joint and product-distribution distinguishers. Their complete human core then performs the simultaneous source, adversary and test-function union bound with explicit entropy and seed-length costs; the difficulty is this new dependency-control construction rather than a routine random-function count.
required_context: Exact Theorem6.1 with natural n,k,m,d,t, Delta>=0, epsilon>0 and the displayed implicit/asymptotic log(n-k) seed bound, whose real-valued logarithm entails n>k. Complete source proof1850–2041 including random-function choice, both Q1/Q2 terms, collision-graph independent-class construction1905–1976, martingale Azuma bounds1977–2009 and full union bound2012–2041. The last seed-size inequality2034 uses n-k+2, so do not promote the display to a new exact n=k endpoint. Noncolluding tuple definitions428–443/861–867 and entropy-preserving class456–461 remain closed context. Underlying seeded-extractor requirement remains exact definition436–443, not a replacement notion. Sibling747 equivalence proof is unqualified context due to documented bad-tuple pool cardinality question; no equivalent/consequence/support extra count.
